questions.stem:
(a) Name four components of blood and state one function of each. [8 marks]
(b) Explain the ABO blood group system and state why blood must be matched before transfusion. [8 marks]
(c) State two reasons why intending couples should know their genotype. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
8 marks: Components with function (2 each): red blood cells - carry oxygen (haemoglobin); white blood cells - fight infection; platelets - blood clotting; plasma - transports nutrients, hormones, wastes, heat
4 marks: ABO: groups A, B, AB, O based on antigens on red cells; corresponding antibodies in plasma (A has anti-B, B has anti-A, O has both, AB has neither)
4 marks: Matching prevents agglutination (clumping) of donor cells by recipient antibodies which can block vessels and cause death; O universal donor, AB universal recipient
4 marks: Two reasons (2 each): to avoid having children with sickle cell disease (AS x AS risk); to make informed choices/counselling; to plan health care
questions.explanation: Blood contains red cells (oxygen), white cells (defence), platelets (clotting) and plasma (transport). ABO groups depend on red-cell antigens and plasma antibodies; mismatched blood agglutinates. Genotype knowledge prevents sickle cell disease in children.

questions.stem:
(a) What are endocrine glands? [2 marks]
(b) Name four endocrine glands, the hormone each produces and one function of the hormone. [12 marks]
(c) State the effect of (i) under-secretion of insulin; (ii) over-secretion of growth hormone in childhood; (iii) under-secretion of thyroxine in children. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Ductless glands that secrete hormones directly into the blood
12 marks: Any four glands with hormone and function (3 each): pituitary - growth hormone - growth; thyroid - thyroxine - regulates metabolism; pancreas (islets) - insulin - lowers blood sugar; adrenal - adrenaline - prepares for emergency; ovary - oestrogen - female characteristics; testis - testosterone - male characteristics
2 marks: Under-secretion of insulin: diabetes mellitus (high blood sugar)
2 marks: Over-secretion of growth hormone in childhood: gigantism
2 marks: Under-secretion of thyroxine in children: cretinism (accept goitre)
questions.explanation: Endocrine glands are ductless and release hormones into blood. Pituitary (growth hormone), thyroid (thyroxine), pancreas (insulin), adrenal (adrenaline). Low insulin: diabetes; excess growth hormone: gigantism; low thyroxine in children: cretinism.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the four types of teeth in humans and state the function of each. [8 marks]
(b) Explain how dental caries develops. [6 marks]
(c) State three ways of preventing dental caries. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
8 marks: Incisors - cutting; canines - tearing; premolars - crushing/grinding; molars - grinding/chewing (2 each)
6 marks: Food particles and sugar remain on teeth; bacteria form plaque and ferment sugar to acid; acid dissolves enamel and dentine forming cavities, leading to pain and infection of the pulp (3 points x 2)
6 marks: Any three (2 each): brush at least twice daily with fluoride toothpaste; reduce sugary foods and drinks between meals; use dental floss; rinse mouth after meals; regular dental check-ups; eat foods rich in calcium
questions.explanation: Incisors cut, canines tear, premolars and molars grind. Plaque bacteria convert sugars to acids that dissolve enamel. Prevent with fluoride brushing, less sugar, flossing and dental check-ups.

questions.stem:
(a) Define the school health programme. [2 marks]
(b) Describe four components of the school health programme. [12 marks]
(c) State three benefits of the school health programme to pupils. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Planned activities and services in school to promote and protect the health of pupils and staff
12 marks: Any four described (3 each): skill-based health education; healthful school environment (safe buildings, water, toilets); school health services (screening, first aid, immunisation); school feeding/nutrition services; school-home-community relationship
6 marks: Any three (2 each): early detection and treatment of defects; prevention of diseases; better attendance and learning; healthy habits for life; safe environment
questions.explanation: The school health programme comprises health education, a healthful environment, health services, nutrition services and school-community links, leading to early detection of defects, disease prevention and better learning.

questions.stem:
(a) Define (i) epidemiology; (ii) vital statistics. [4 marks]
(b) A local government area had a mid-year population of 120,000. In that year there were 4,200 live births, 1,080 deaths and 147 deaths of infants under one year. Calculate: (i) the crude birth rate; (ii) the crude death rate; (iii) the infant mortality rate. [12 marks]
(c) State two uses of vital statistics. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Epidemiology: study of the distribution and determinants of diseases and health events in populations
2 marks: Vital statistics: records/data on births, deaths, marriages, diseases in a population
4 marks: CBR = 4,200/120,000 x 1,000 = 35 per 1,000 population
4 marks: CDR = 1,080/120,000 x 1,000 = 9 per 1,000 population
4 marks: IMR = 147/4,200 x 1,000 = 35 per 1,000 live births
4 marks: Any two (2 each): planning health services; measuring health status of the population; evaluating programmes; allocating resources; research
questions.explanation: Epidemiology studies disease patterns; vital statistics record births and deaths. CBR = 35 per 1,000; CDR = 9 per 1,000; IMR = 147/4,200 x 1,000 = 35 per 1,000 live births. Uses: planning and evaluation.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four sources of water supply in a community. [4 marks]
(b) Describe the stages in the purification of water for a town supply. [10 marks]
(c) State three ways of making water safe for drinking at home. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: Any four (1 each): rain; river/stream; well; borehole; spring; lake/pond; pipe-borne
2 marks: Storage/screening: water stored in reservoirs; large objects screened out
2 marks: Coagulation/sedimentation: alum added, particles settle
2 marks: Filtration through sand beds
2 marks: Chlorination/disinfection to kill germs
2 marks: Storage in covered tanks and distribution through pipes
6 marks: Any three (2 each): boiling and cooling; filtering; adding chlorine/water purifying tablets; storing in clean covered containers; solar disinfection
questions.explanation: Sources include rain, rivers, wells, boreholes and springs. Town purification: screening and storage, coagulation and sedimentation with alum, filtration, chlorination, distribution. At home: boil, filter, chlorinate and store covered.

questions.stem:
(a) State three aims of first aid. [3 marks]
(b) List five items in a first aid box. [5 marks]
(c) Describe the first aid treatment for (i) severe bleeding from the forearm; (ii) a scald from boiling water. [12 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Preserve life; prevent the condition from becoming worse; promote recovery (1 each)
5 marks: Any five (1 each): bandages; sterile dressings; adhesive plasters; cotton wool; antiseptic; scissors; disposable gloves; safety pins; triangular bandage
6 marks: Bleeding: wear gloves; apply direct pressure with a clean pad; raise the arm above heart level; apply firm bandage; add more pads if blood soaks through; treat for shock and get medical help
6 marks: Scald: cool under clean running water for at least 10-20 minutes; remove rings/tight items before swelling; do not burst blisters or apply oil/toothpaste; cover with clean non-fluffy dressing or cling film; seek medical help for large burns
questions.explanation: First aid aims to preserve life, prevent worsening and promote recovery. For bleeding: direct pressure, elevation, dressing, treat shock. For scalds: cool with running water, remove rings, cover loosely, no oils or bursting blisters.

questions.stem:
(a) Name three harmful components of tobacco smoke and state the effect of each. [6 marks]
(b) State four effects of excessive alcohol consumption on health. [8 marks]
(c) Suggest three ways of reducing drug abuse among secondary school students. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: Nicotine - addiction, raises heart rate/blood pressure; tar - cancer of lungs/mouth/throat; carbon monoxide - reduces oxygen carried by blood (2 each)
8 marks: Any four (2 each): liver cirrhosis; stomach ulcers; impaired judgement leading to accidents; addiction; brain damage/memory loss; heart disease; malnutrition; family and social problems
6 marks: Any three (2 each): drug education in schools; guidance and counselling; positive peer groups and clubs; enforcement of laws/NDLEA; parental supervision; recreation and sports
questions.explanation: Nicotine is addictive, tar causes cancer and CO lowers oxygen transport. Alcohol damages the liver, stomach, brain and judgement. Reduce abuse through education, counselling, sports, parental care and law enforcement.

questions.stem:
With reference to malaria:
(a) name the causative organism and the vector; [4 marks]
(b) describe how the disease is transmitted; [4 marks]
(c) state four signs and symptoms; [4 marks]
(d) state four methods of prevention and control. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Causative organism: Plasmodium (protozoan), e.g. Plasmodium falciparum
2 marks: Vector: female Anopheles mosquito
4 marks: An infected female Anopheles bites a person and injects sporozoites with saliva; parasites multiply in liver and red blood cells; a mosquito biting an infected person picks up gametocytes and continues the cycle
4 marks: Any four (1 each): fever; chills and shivering; headache; joint pains; vomiting; loss of appetite; anaemia; sweating
8 marks: Any four (2 each): sleeping under insecticide-treated nets; clearing stagnant water and bushes; insecticide spraying; window/door nets; insect repellents; prompt treatment with antimalarials (ACTs); preventive treatment for pregnant women
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium and carried by the female Anopheles mosquito. Symptoms include fever, chills, headache and joint pain. Prevent with treated nets, removing breeding sites, insecticides and prompt treatment.

questions.stem:
(a) What is family planning? [2 marks]
(b) State four reasons why family planning is necessary. [8 marks]
(c) Describe two methods each of (i) modern and (ii) natural family planning. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Deciding the number and spacing of children by a couple using acceptable methods
8 marks: Any four (2 each): protects the health of mother and child; allows proper spacing; enables parents to provide for children; reduces maternal deaths; manageable family size; helps national planning
6 marks: Modern methods (any two, 3 each): condom; oral pills; injectables; implants; intra-uterine device; sterilisation (vasectomy/tubal ligation)
4 marks: Natural methods (any two, 2 each): calendar/rhythm method; withdrawal; lactational amenorrhoea; cervical mucus/basal temperature method; abstinence
questions.explanation: Family planning is deciding the number and spacing of children. It protects maternal and child health and allows adequate care. Modern: condom, pills, injectables, IUD; natural: calendar, cervical mucus, lactational amenorrhoea.
